---
title: "Literature"
---


Every entry here was checked against Crossref before it went on the page:
authors, title, venue, DOI. Nothing was copied out of another bibliography.
Three candidate DOIs were dropped during that check because they resolved to
an entirely different paper than the one intended, which is the whole reason
for doing it.

Where a work has no DOI, and older textbooks often do not, this page says so
rather than pairing the title with an identifier that points somewhere else.

The list is grouped by the question each source answers, because that is how
it grew: most design decisions in qdaR are arguments about method, and these
are the sources behind them.


## Agreement between coders

These are the papers behind the six coefficients. Cohen and Fleiss tell you
what the numbers are; Feinstein and Cicchetti tell you why reporting only one
of them is a bad idea.

## Saturation, and the argument about it

The saturation number this package reports is *code* saturation and nothing
else. The last two entries are the objections, and they belong in any report
that quotes the figure.

Qualitative Research in Sport, Exercise and Health. | [10.1080/2159676x.2019.1704846](https://doi.org/10.1080/2159676x.2019.1704846) |

## Works without a DOI

* [Cramér, H. (1946). *Mathematical Methods of Statistics*. Princeton
  University Press.]{#litref-Cramer1946Mathematical} Where the *V* reported by `qda_chisq()` comes from.
* [Sokal, R. R., & Sneath, P. H. A. (1963). *Principles of Numerical
  Taxonomy*. Freeman.]{#litref-SokalSneath1963Principles} Average linkage, the default used here.
* [Wilkinson, L. (2005). *The Grammar of Graphics* (2nd ed.). Springer.]{#litref-Wilkinson2005Grammar} The
  book the plotting backends descend from.
* [REFI-QDA Standard]{#litref-RefiQda}, <https://www.qdasoftware.org/>. The interchange format
  zotQDA reads and writes. Not this package's concern, but it explains where
  a few column names come from.

::: {.callout-note title="One reference that is deliberately missing"}

There is no established measure of agreement between whole *category
systems*. Kappa and alpha both assume the coders already share one flat
set of categories, which is exactly what is in dispute while a codebook
is still being built. `qda_level_agreement()` flattens the hierarchy
level by level and recomputes, a workaround, not a citation.
:::
